# Tether snags

Small survey drones that fly on a hair-thin fibre tether can snag on cranes, rigging and power lines near a port. A snagged tether cuts the drone link and can drop the drone on a working quay. The tether is almost invisible to a camera at range, so crews learn about it only after the snag.

Open questions: how far out a tether can be seen, and which cue shows it first.
